changelog:
What you'll see with this update:
• Alert email now sends via a Gmail account (cytechalerts@gmail.com) instead of the old mail server -- live-tested delivering both the support copy and the owner copy.
• Config self-healing reliability fix: the automatic repair for a damaged settings file now runs on its own, independently of Home Assistant -- so it also works in the rare case where the file is too damaged for the system to start up normally (previously it could miss exactly that case).
• Update reliability: files now come from a version-pinned source, so an update can never half-install again (a unit could previously show the new version while still running old settings, and then refuse to re-apply).
• 'Config Check' row: the result shows just ok / restored / error / waiting -- no trailing number (it was an internal timestamp).
• The settings row 'Boots' is now 'Warnings' (in future it can carry alerts other than booting, too): it reads 'Repeated restarts' instead of the cryptic 'RESTART_STORM', with a plain-English message ('The unit restarted N times in the last 24h... please contact Cytech Support.'). The guard itself is unchanged: it flags 5+ restarts in 24h so Cytech can help.
• Config self-healing: if the main settings file is ever damaged, the unit repairs it from the last known-good copy and tells you (popup + email).
• A 'Config Check' row in the settings screen, refreshed right after every restart and every 4 hours.
• A clean alert-email setup: your address field is 'My Email for Alerts'; Register shows its result on screen; alerts always reach Cytech Support too, with your address copied automatically.
details:
44c (fix revision, bench-only -- not yet fleet-committed) corrects a mistake in 44b: the .cytech_secrets rollout caveat was originally placed in the owner-facing warnings array (shown verbatim on the customer's pre-update popup), but an owner cannot act on it -- they have no way to edit CY_SMTP_USER/CY_SMTP_PASS themselves. Moved to this operator-only details field instead; warnings array is now empty.

OPERATOR NOTE, DO NOT SHIP BEYOND THE BENCH UNIT: do not promote this version or push it to any device in the field until every target device's .cytech_secrets has been updated to the new Gmail account by an operator (SSH), or a proper automated rollout mechanism exists.

44b (fix revision, bench-only -- not yet fleet-committed) adds one more change on top of 44a: cytech_email_gen.py's two smtp notify platforms (cytech_alert_support, cytech_alert_email) now point at smtp.gmail.com/port 465/tls with sender cytechalerts@gmail.com, replacing mail.server282.com/ucmapi@cytech.biz. Reason: the old account's credentials were a single shared plaintext secret (CY_SMTP_USER/CY_SMTP_PASS in .cytech_secrets) reused across every unit with no per-device isolation and no rotation path; Gmail's App Passwords give each device its own revocable credential under one account. Live-tested on the bench unit 2026-09-06: both notify.cytech_alert_support and notify.cytech_alert_email confirmed delivering to support@cytech.biz and the CY_SMTP_RECIPIENT address respectively, no SMTP/auth errors in Core logs. IMPORTANT CAVEAT, not yet resolved: .cytech_secrets is device-local and never touched by updates, so a device that pulls this code change without ALSO getting CY_SMTP_USER/CY_SMTP_PASS updated to the new Gmail account+app-password will have its alert emails silently break (its old server282 password will not authenticate against Gmail). This is safe on the bench unit only because its .cytech_secrets was updated by hand alongside this change; a real fleet rollout needs a plan for updating every device's secrets in lockstep with the code, not yet designed.

44a (fix revision, bench-only -- not yet fleet-committed) fixes a gap found by a live corruption test on the bench unit (2026-09-06) in the v42/v43 config self-heal: cytech_integrity_check.py (the runtime companion to check_config_integrity in first_boot.sh) was only ever invoked by a homeassistant.start-triggered automation living in automations.yaml/configuration.yaml. But a configuration.yaml corrupted badly enough to fail parsing is exactly what puts HA Core into Safe Mode, and Safe Mode does not load custom automations -- so the ONE case this whole feature exists for (configuration.yaml too broken to load) was exactly the case where the checker was never called. Reproduced live: a truncated configuration.yaml left the bench unit stuck in Safe Mode with no restore, no alert, no email; recovered manually. THE FIX: new ensure_config_integrity_watcher() in first_boot.sh, same pattern as the existing ensure_reset_watcher, registers a nohup polling loop (5-minute interval) as an SSH addon init_command -- so cytech_integrity_check.py now runs from inside the SSH addon container, independent of whether HA Core can parse configuration.yaml at all. Prior watcher entries are matched and replaced by a stable substring ('cytech_integrity_check.py'), the same de-dup approach the reset watcher uses, so existing units pick up the fix in place rather than accumulating duplicate loops.

v43 is the fleet-wide release of the v42 series (v42 plus fix-revisions 42a-42f, which only ever ran on the bench unit); 42a was an early rename-only attempt and 42d was a same-content re-ship for a delivery problem, so neither appears as a change below. What v43 shipped:
(1) CDN-proof downloads. raw.githubusercontent.com serves each URL from a CDN with max-age=300, keyed by the URL itself (a query string does NOT create a separate entry -- verified 2026-09-04), so a device downloading right after a release could be served the PREVIOUS version's file with no error, then write the new version label -- silently half-updated, and permanently unable to re-apply ('the units can never pull the real package, because the checker considers it up to date'). The bench unit hit exactly that during the 42c release. THE FIX: every release is git-tagged with its version and files are downloaded from the tag URL -- a URL no device has ever fetched, so it can never be served from cache. The manifest itself stays on the branch URL (stale reads there are harmless: 'up to date' for at most 5 minutes, then the next check is fresh). .cytech_secrets.example documents that CYTECH_MANIFEST_URL must not be pinned to a tag (the tag changes every release).
(2) cytech_integrity_check.py writes the status word only ('ok'), not 'ok <epoch>' -- the epoch leaked onto the Config Check dashboard row as an unexplained number.
(3) The boot guard state RESTART_STORM became REPEATED_RESTARTS with plain-English messages ('Repeated restarts detected' popup/email; message 'The unit restarted N times in the last 24h (first at HH:MM:SS local). Repeated restarts usually mean a problem -- please contact Cytech Support.'). Automation id cytech_alert_boot_storm is unchanged. (3b) The sensor 'Cytech Boot Status' is renamed 'Cytech Warning' -- the row is expected to carry other warnings besides boot/restart ones -- and its unique_id is bumped to cytech_warning_result_sensor on purpose: the entity registry pins an entity_id at first registration, so a name change alone would NOT move the id. A bumped unique_id re-registers every unit fresh as sensor.cytech_warning; units that already ran v35+ keep the orphaned sensor.cytech_boot_status (unreferenced, harmless). The on-disk result file (/config/.cytech_boot_result) and the dashboard row's message attribute are unchanged.
(4) The runtime integrity check also runs right after every core start (boot AND update restarts), not just every 4 hours, so the Config Check row shows its real result within minutes instead of 'unknown' for up to 4 hours after an update restart; before the first run ever it reads 'waiting' instead of HA's error-lookalike 'unknown'.
(5) Config self-healing: the system keeps a rolling known-good snapshot of configuration.yaml (refreshed after every clean check), and if the live file is ever found corrupt it is replaced by the snapshot with the broken copy saved as configuration.yaml.corrupt.<timestamp>, HA restarts, and the integrity alert says so. Two safety properties: the snapshot is only refreshed after the configuration actually parsed clean, so a corrupted state can never be snapshotted as 'good'; and no restore happens unless the snapshot itself parses, so there is no restore loop. Integrity alerts are emailed (support@cytech.biz always, plus the owner's registered address per the v41 rule), and the System Health dashboard shows a Config Check row with the last running check result. For v39 or older, 44a also carries v40 and v41: the owner's address field is 'My Email for Alerts', a Register press always reports its status on screen (empty field: 'Enter your email first, then press Register.'), a successful Register sends ONE confirmation mail To: the owner Cc: support@cytech.biz, alerts ALWAYS go to support@cytech.biz with the owner's registered address copied automatically (no Cytech/Me/Both selector), and units with mail configured but no owner registered yet show a small non-blocking hint. Nothing is lost if the owner never registers: support@cytech.biz always receives every alert.
